rules.title: Source of income discrimination prohibition (FEHA)
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not refuse to rent to someone, or apply different terms, because of how the tenant will pay rent (source of income), including Housing Choice (Section 8) vouchers and other rental assistance. They also may not refuse to complete required program paperwork or advertise limits such as "No Section 8."
rules.coverage_text: Most providers of housing and housing-related services, such as landlords, tenant screening companies, property management companies and real estate agents, for most housing accommodations in California.
rules.exemptions: According to the excerpt, an owner who occupies a home and rents to one additional person may exclude applicants based on protected characteristics, but still cannot make, print, or publish discriminatory statements, notices, or advertisements.
rules.penalty: Remedies include recovery of out-of-pocket losses, an injunction, access to housing that was denied, damages for emotional distress, civil penalties or punitive damages, and attorney's fees.
rules.quoted_span: No. California law protects tenants from discrimination based on how a tenant will be paying rent (“source of income”). This includes the State of California’s COVID-19 Rent Relief Program, Housing Choice (Section 8) vouchers, (SSI) social security disability benefits, or wages earned from a job.

rules.title: Criminal history screening limits (FEHA)
rules.requirement: Housing providers may check an applicant's criminal history, but may not consider arrests that did not lead to a conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile justice records, and may not have blanket bans on all people with a criminal history. A denial based on a conviction must be directly related to the applicant's ability to be a good tenant and not be a threat to health, safety or property.
rules.coverage_text: Housing providers, including tenant screening companies, screening applicants for housing in California.
rules.penalty: Remedies include recovery of out-of-pocket losses, an injunction, access to housing that was denied, damages for emotional distress, civil penalties or punitive damages, and attorney's fees.
rules.quoted_span: Housing  providers cannot consider some types of criminal history including arrests that did not lead to a conviction, records that are sealed or expunged, or records or matters processed in the juvenile justice system. Housing providers are also prohibited from having “blanket bans” of all people with a criminal history.
